reasoning_traces.think:
The core mechanism of dynamic Bayesian quantile synthesis (BPS) operates by aggregating agent predictive densities into a single coherent forecast distribution. Each agent j provides a predictive density h_{tj}(f_{tj}), which is integrated against a synthesis kernel α(y_t|f_t,Φ_t) that depends on time-varying parameters Φ_t. The synthesis function α encodes how agent outputs are combined, typically through a weighted average or regression framework. This approach allows for heterogeneity among agents while maintaining a unified probabilistic forecast. In the factor-augmented version, regression coefficients θ_{itj} are modeled as linear combinations of latent factors u_{tj} with loadings λ_{ij}, reducing dimensionality and capturing cross-series dependencies. The use of asymmetric Laplace (AL) likelihood ensures that the resulting quantile estimates are consistent with Bayesian principles, even though it is a working likelihood rather than a true posterior. The model’s state-space formulation enables recursive updating via Gibbs sampling, incorporating forward-filtering backward-sampling (FFBS) for latent states and generalized Bayesian random walk (GBRW) updates for scale parameters. These components together support robust, adaptive forecasting under uncertainty, particularly in macroeconomic contexts where structural shifts are common.
